title: Espaces stratifiés et voisinages côniques (ou : déploiement des espaces stratifiés) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. In these notes Grothendieck axiomatises the 'unfolding' (déploiement) of a tame stratified space. It is encoded as a system Σ*(d) of spaces indexed by finite non-empty totally ordered sets d = {0,...,d}. Σ*(0) = Σ is a manifold with boundary and corners. Σ*(1) is the space of 'first-order boundary data', with maps source and but (target) to Σ*(0). Strictly increasing maps between ordinals induce maps between the Σ*(d). The previous page lists conditions (c) 'intrinsicness', i.e. the source map is proper and fibrant, and (d) 'non-singularity', i.e. Σ*(0) is a manifold with boundary and the 'bord' map Σ*(1) → Σ*(0) has the boundary as image.

On this page he sharpens condition (b) into a local description of corners. It is the familiar structure of the iterated boundaries of a manifold with corners, but with the faces labelled by an ordered set.

(b1) Fix x ∈ Σ = Σ*(0). The points z_α ∈ Σ*(1) over x under but: Σ*(1) → Σ*(0) correspond bijectively to the local boundary hyperface germs B_α of Σ at x. These germs are the images under b of the germs of Σ*(1) at the z_α. So Σ*(1) → Σ is the 'normalisation' of the boundary, an immersion that separates the local branches of the boundary.

(b2) Let n = card{z_α}, the corner depth of x. There is a unique point x̃ ∈ Σ*(n) over x whose images under the n maps φ_{i,n}: Σ*(n) → Σ*(1), i = 0,...,n−1, are exactly the z_α. These maps are induced by the increasing maps Δ_1 → Δ_n with image {i,n}. Hence the n local faces at x are canonically totally ordered. In the unfolding of a stratified space they are labelled by the distinct strata of a flag S_0 < ... < S_n. Each B_α is a codimension-1 boundary stratum through x.

(b3) For 1 ≤ d ≤ n, consider the 'last vertex' map Σ*(d) → Σ*(0) induced by {d} ↪ {0,...,d}. The points of Σ*(d) over x correspond bijectively to:
- the d-element subsets of the set I of germs B_α;
- equivalently, the d-element subsets of the set of z_α;
- equivalently, the elements of P_d([0,...,n−1]).
The correspondence works as follows. A subset A determines the unique increasing map Δ_d → Δ_n with image A ∪ {n}. The induced map Σ*(n) → Σ*(d) sends x̃ to the corresponding point. The next page adds that the image of the germ of Σ*(d) at that point is the intersection of the B_α, α ∈ A. It then restricts to 'cofinal' strictly increasing maps (those preserving the last element). This identifies the indexing category with ordinals with an adjoined last element ω, i.e. an augmented semi-simplicial structure.

So the page states the corner-counting axiom: locally Σ*(d) over a depth-n corner has C(n,d) points, indexed by d-faces. This makes Σ*(•) the semi-simplicial 'face system' of a manifold with corners whose hyperfaces are compatibly ordered. It is essentially an ⟨n⟩-manifold structure.

Purpose: to characterise intrinsically which systems of manifolds with corners arise as unfoldings of stratified spaces with conical neighbourhoods. This is the 'théorème de déploiement' programme of the Esquisse.
errors: No genuine mathematical error. Uniqueness of x̃ in (b2) and the bijection in (b3) require that the local faces at x carry distinct labels, so that they are totally ordered. That ordering is not stated on this page; it holds in the unfolding because faces correspond to distinct strata of a flag.

Notational drift: the previous page uses 'source' as the proper fibrant map and 'bord' as the boundary immersion; this page uses 'but' (b) for the map whose fibres are the z_α. The roles are consistent only if 'but' here is the same map as 'bord' there. This is plausible given the last-vertex convention, but not explicit.
'Σ^n(n)' in the diagram is a slip for Σ*(n).

ideas.what: Σ*(1) → Σ as a normalisation of the boundary: points over x correspond to local boundary hyperface germs
ideas.modern_name: boundary ∂X of a manifold with corners as an immersed manifold (Douady/Joyce convention)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Douady (1961), Cerf; systematised by Joyce (2009–) and Melrose

ideas.what: Points of Σ*(d) over a depth-n corner correspond to d-subsets of local faces; the germ image is the intersection of the corresponding faces
ideas.modern_name: iterated boundaries ∂^k X / face poset of a manifold with corners

ideas.what: Faces at each corner are canonically totally ordered (labelled by strata), encoded by a semi-simplicial system indexed by ordinals with cofinal (last-element-preserving) maps
ideas.modern_name: ⟨n⟩-manifolds / manifolds with ordered faces; unzipping of conically smooth stratified spaces
ideas.usually_credited_to: Jänich (1968), Laures (2000) for ⟨n⟩-manifolds; Ayala–Francis–Tanaka (2017) for unzipping; Verona (1984) and Brasselet–Hector–Saralegi (1991) for resolutions/dépliement
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), §5 on tame topology, sketches the déploiement idea without these axioms

ideas.what: Axiomatisation of the unfolding of a stratified space as a functor from finite ordinals (cofinal injections) to manifolds with corners satisfying corner-counting and fibrancy conditions
ideas.modern_name: resolution/unfolding of Thom–Mather stratified spaces; décollement diagram
ideas.where_published: only sketched in Esquisse d'un programme

missed.claim: Grothendieck's axioms present the unfolding as an augmented semi-simplicial diagram of manifolds with corners indexed by ordinals with cofinal maps, with an exact local corner count. This is very close to Ayala–Francis–Tanaka's unzipping of conically smooth stratified spaces and to ⟨n⟩-manifolds. The explicit combinatorial axiom (fibre of Σ*(d) over a depth-n point ≅ P_d([0,n−1]) via maps Δ_d → Δ_n with image A ∪ {n}) offers a characterisation of 'which systems come from stratified spaces'. It is a converse direction not stated in this form in the literature, as far as I know.
missed.quote: les points de Σ*(d) au dessus de x sont en correspondance biunivoque avec l'une des parties de card d ... en associant à telle partie A l'application croissante unique de Δ_d = {0,…,d} en Δ_n ... d'image A ∪ {n}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It could give an intrinsic, purely combinatorial-plus-manifold-with-corners characterisation of conically smooth / tame stratified spaces. This would be relevant to exit-path ∞-categories and stratified homotopy theory (Ayala–Francis–Tanaka, Nocera–Volpe, Haine).

deep.surprise_reason: The local mathematics is standard manifold-with-corners combinatorics. Interest lies in the unpublished, fairly precise axiomatic form of the déploiement programme only sketched in the Esquisse, which anticipates the structure of later 'unzipping' constructions.
